statement: Find all triples $(x, y, p)$ of positive integers with $p$ prime, $p = x^2 + 1$, and $2p^2 = y^2 + 1$.

Convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $\angle B = \angle D = 90^\circ$ and $AB > AD$. $P \in AB$ with $AP = AD$. Lines $PD$ and $BC$ meet at $Q$. Perpendicular from $Q$ to $AC$ meets $AB$ at $R$. $S$ = foot of perpendicular from $D$ to $AC$. Prove $\angle PSQ = \angle RCP$.

A water city has platforms connected by bridges. A move: if $AB$ and $AC$ exist but $BC$ doesn't, replace $AB$ by $BC$. A configuration is \textit{good} if the city is connected. Starting from any good configuration, prove any other good configuration with the same number of bridges can be reached using only allowed moves.

Luffy has a box with number $X$ and a machine. Opening a box adds $X$ to score and destroys it. Putting $X$ in the machine gives two boxes: $X+1$ and $X-1$. Start with score 0 and one box containing 0. (a) Prove Luffy can guarantee score $\geq 1000$. (b) Can Luffy guarantee score $\geq 10^6$ while never going below $-42$?
Find all nonneg­ative reals $\alpha$ for which there exists $f : \mathbb{R}^+ \to \mathbb{R}^+$ with $f(x^\alpha + y) = (f(x+y))^\alpha + f(y)$ for all $x, y > 0$.

In acute $\triangle ABC$ with $AB + BC = 4AC$, $D \in AC$ is the foot of the bisector from $B$. $P, Q \in BD$ with $BP = 2DQ$. The perpendicular from $Q$ to $BD$ meets $AB$ and $BC$ at $X, Y$. Line $L$ through $P$ parallel to $AC$; $B$ is on the opposite side of $L$ from $X, Y$. An ant goes $X \to $ (point on $AC$) $\to$ (point on $L$) $\to$ (point on $AC$) $\to Y$. Prove the minimum path length is $4XY$.
